top_choice_rationale: P001 (Katori and Ye, optical lattice clock) is the only slate entry where achievement, maturity and credit all hold together: one concept (the magic wavelength) and one demonstrated result (10^-18 uncertainty), reproduced in several laboratories and species, with a two-name allocation that no proposal disputes. The remaining reservation is that it reads as a measurement advance beside the 2005 and 2012 prizes. I rank the experiment-only B001 trio (P005) next because it avoids the theory-credit overlap with B011, then the mixed trio (P004); the Higgs trio (P002) and the moire trio (P003) follow, and no award last since mature, creditable candidates exist.
recusal_note: No documented connection to Katori or Ye; my research stay in John Hall's laboratory is background lineage for the clock field only and is disclosed for transparency. Slate entries on light-matter quantum memories (B003) would be close to my own rare-earth-crystal quantum-memory work, but none is on this slate. No specific conflict apparent from profile for B001, B020 or B041.
